subject.title: CLI deadline re-runs an already-accepted prompt on a gateway-fallback session (duplicate-write hazard)

question: After a Gateway-accepted CLI turn exceeds the caller deadline, should the CLI keep tracking and return an in-flight accepted-run result, or may it fall back only after successfully aborting that accepted run?
rationale: Both choices affect the public CLI timeout contract, liveness expectations, and whether callers can safely recover a long-running turn; source evidence supports avoiding a second execution but does not establish the intended user-facing timeout behavior.

options.title: Return accepted-run timeout state
options.body: Preserve the accepted Gateway run and return an explicit in-flight timeout result containing its run/session identity for callers to reattach or poll.

options.title: Abort before fallback
options.body: Retain embedded fallback only when the Gateway confirms that the accepted run was aborted, with the abort outcome surfaced to the caller.

options.title: Remove embedded fallback
options.body: Make CLI deadline expiry terminal after Gateway acceptance and require a later explicit reattach command or invocation.

recommendation.title: Return accepted-run timeout state
recommendation.body: Preserve the accepted Gateway run and return an explicit in-flight timeout result containing its run/session identity for callers to reattach or poll.

likelyOwner.reason: The reporter has the only supplied production observations that distinguish a recoverable in-flight contract from an abort-before-fallback contract.
